imagePrompt: A teenage right-handed girl on the fairway is practising her swing with an iron, her ball accidentally moved slightly from its spot.
imageAlt: Teen girl with an iron on the fairway, ball displaced by a practice swing.

issues: Golfer is not addressing the ball with a left-handed posture—the stance, club grip, and direction appear right-handed, contradicting the requirement for a left-handed golfer.
The club and ball are otherwise accurate, but the golfer's handedness is essential to match the prompt correction.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Ensure the teenage girl is addressing the ball as a left-handed golfer: her right hand is the lowest on the grip, her right side is closest to the target, and her stance faces opposite that of a right-handed golfer. Adjust her body orientation and grip accordingly.

questions.title: Ball moves when you practise your swing
questions.question: You are on the fairway (the short grass before the green). You take a practice swing and accidentally hit your ball and it moves. What should you do?

choices.text: Put the ball back where it was and add one extra shot to your score
Put the ball back with no extra shots
Play the ball from where it rolled to
Drop a different ball and add an extra shot

questions.explanation: If you accidentally move your ball while practising your swing on the fairway, you must put it back where it was and count one extra shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short grass part between the tee and the green.
A swing you make to get ready, but you don’t try to hit the ball.

questions.teachingTip: Many players move the ball by accident. Remind children to always watch their ball when practising a swing.
likelyMisconceptions: Some might think they can just play the ball from where it stops.
Some might forget to add the extra shot.

questions.title: Ball moved while preparing a stroke
questions.question: If you accidentally move your ball when taking a practice swing on the fairway (not on the tee or green), what is the correct action?

choices.text: Replace the ball and add a one-stroke penalty
Replace the ball with no penalty
Play the ball from its new place
Drop a new ball and add a penalty stroke

questions.explanation: If you move your ball by accident during a practice swing away from the teeing area or green, you must replace it and add a one-stroke penalty.
